where: Vyro Music is a working prototype, not a finished product. The server (accounts, uploads, streaming, review and copyright checks, statistics, recommendations, lyrics) is built and has been run: its 166 automated checks pass, including checks with real audio files. The app (listening and mixing, library, playlists, queue, lyrics, the artist Studio and the admin console) is written, with automated checks of its own, but none of it has been run yet on a phone or a computer.
So "Built" in this document means written and ready to be tested, not proven. The first real milestone is to run the setup script and the app's checks on your machine and fix what they find.

Nothing can be opened to the public yet. What stands in the way is listed below: outside services to connect, legal documents, store accounts and hosting, and the launch-level features that are still missing.

Launch-level features still missing: YouTube search and playback, album pages and albums (Vyro has none yet), browsing by mood, activity, decade and language, sharing and deep links, blocking and reporting users, accessibility, translations and an onboarding tour, resumable uploads and release types, claiming an artist profile, and almost all of the operations work (environments, monitoring, backups, beta, support, store listings).

working.text: Sign up and log in with email (with confirmation) or a phone code, Google and Apple sign-in on the server side, guest mode, age rules with parent consent, password reset, a saved login, a profile with photo, country and language, privacy controls (private session, sharing your country with artists, personalization), a download of your data, and account deletion that removes every file.
Upgrade a listener account to an artist account, upload songs (MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV, OGG, AIFF, up to 300 MB), cover art, loudness measured at upload, and submit a song for release.

Copies of songs already on Vyro are caught by audio fingerprint, a reviewer queue with approve, reject and bulk actions, copyright notices with counter-notices, automatic suspension after three upheld notices, roles (listener, moderator, admin) and an audit log.
Songs stream from short-lived secure links and can be played from any point. Explicit songs are hidden from guests and from anyone who turned them off.

Normal and Mixing modes with crossfades, shuffle and repeat, a queue (play next, reorder, remove, history), swipe gestures, picking up where you left off after the app was closed, a buffering spinner with automatic retries, and lock-screen controls.

Scan folders on the device, read tags, browse by songs, albums, artists, genres and folders, leave folders out, ignore short clips, like any song (on the device or on Vyro, saved on the server for signed-in people), and delete a song from the device.
Create and edit playlists with a cover picture, mix songs from your own files and from Vyro, drag to reorder, sort, select several songs, and remove duplicates.

Artists add synced or plain lyrics in the Studio. Listeners see the current line highlighted. Songs on the device use a .lrc file next to them or lyrics stored inside. Listeners can report wrong lyrics.

Home shows Continue listening, picks from the taste picker, what is popular in your country, and lists chosen by staff, with "Not interested" and a reset. Search finds songs and artists even with typos, with suggestions, recent searches and browsing by genre. Artist pages (with follow) and charts of songs, artists and rising artists.
An artist dashboard (plays, listeners, audience split, per-song listening, countries) and a listener profile, both filled by real plays recorded by the app.
For reviewers: the review queue, copyright notices, and artist management (verify, suspend, restore).

blockers.why: Phone sign-in codes only print on the server's screen until a provider is connected.
Confirmation, password reset and parent-consent emails also only print on the server's screen.
The sign-in buttons say "not set up" until client IDs and the sign-in plugins are added.

blockers.what: A copyright lookup service you may use commercially
blockers.why: Matching against music released elsewhere is connected but switched off. The free AcoustID service is for non-commercial use only; a commercial app needs an agreement with them or a paid service.

The terms, privacy policy and artist agreement are placeholders. The age limits, the copyright notice wording and time limits, music licensing and royalty reporting, and the "Vyro Music" name all need a lawyer for each launch market.

blockers.what: Apple and Google store accounts, and push services
blockers.why: Store policy checks, store listings, and push notifications cannot start without them.
The server keeps files on its own disk and has no deployment set-up, monitoring, backups or content delivery network yet.
Audio focus for calls, lock-screen controls, folder access and background audio on Android and iOS, and the speed and size targets, can only be confirmed on devices.
YouTube search and playback are not started, and the requirements demand a compliance review before every release.
The seed catalog and the closed beta need people, not code.

report.unverified: The app's automated checks are written for every feature but have never been run, because the build tools for the app (Flutter) are not available where this was developed. Expect some compile errors and a few failing checks on the first run; they are normally quick to fix. Until then, treat every Built item that involves the app as unconfirmed. The server side is different: it has been run, and its checks pass.
risks: Nobody reviews lyrics. An artist could add lyrics they do not own, and reports from listeners reach the artist, not a moderator.
Anyone can send a copyright notice, and the song goes offline at once. Decide how rights holders are verified before relying on this.
Every uploaded song waits for a reviewer by default, so moderators are needed before artists start uploading.
Playlists, the queue and the listening history are kept on the device only. They are not saved to the server, so they are lost with the phone.
A country with listening on fewer than five songs shows the whole-of-Vyro popular list instead of its own.
On newer Android versions the system may refuse to delete music files that are outside the app's own folder.
Crashes, speed, install size and availability are not measured anywhere yet, so none of the performance targets is confirmed.
Accessibility, translations and the onboarding tour are launch requirements and are not started.
The artist age limit of 18 is a cautious default that needs legal confirmation in each market.

AUTH-02.note: Sign-up, log-in and email confirmation work and the screens are built. Confirmation emails are not actually sent yet: an email service still needs to be connected.

AUTH-06.note: Name, photo, username, country and language. A listener's photo is private to them; an artist's photo is part of their public page. The language picker saves the choice, but Vyro is not translated yet.

AUTH-08.note: Deleting an account needs the typed word DELETE and the password. Plays already counted for artists are kept, without the person's name. Every file goes too: songs, covers and the profile photo.

AUTH-11.note: The sign-up checkbox records which version of the terms was accepted, and when. The legal text itself is a placeholder.

AUTH-12.note: Several devices can be signed in at once and the saved login renews itself. Syncing library and settings is not built.

ART-01.note: Upgrading a listener account to an artist account works, and the "Become an artist" screen is built.

ART-02.note: Top-bar switch between the listener tabs and the artist tabs.

ART-03.note: Name, type, bio, genres and links are stored. Photo and banner are missing.

ART-04.note: Solo, group, producer/DJ and label/manager on the upgrade screen, stored and checked by the server.

ART-05.note: A tick box on the upgrade screen; the declaration is stored with the time it was made.

ART-06.note: The agreement version is recorded and a draft agreement is shown. The real text needs legal review.

ART-08.note: Look-alike names (letter case, spaces, punctuation, accents) are blocked. A reporting flow is missing.

ART-09.note: Artists use the same app and library. Using their listening for recommendations is not built.

ART-11.note: Moderators can mark an artist verified, and verified artists can skip review under the "new artists" policy.

STU-03.note: Title, genre, explicit, allow-blending and length are stored. Featured artists, mood, language, release date, credits and ISRC are missing.

LIB-01.note: Scans the Music and Download folders (Android), the Music folder (desktop) and any folder you add; only changed files are re-read. Automatic background rescans are missing.

LIB-02.note: mp3, m4a, aac, flac, wav, ogg, opus and aiff files are picked up.

LIB-03.note: Tags are read. Cover art is not.

LIB-04.note: Browse by songs, albums, artists, genres and folders. Genres and folders open to their songs, which play from there.

LIB-05.note: Leave a folder out (its songs go at once and stay out when the device is scanned again) and include it again; choose how short a song can be and still be kept (keep everything, 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 or 2 minutes). Both are in Library settings.

LIB-07.note: A heart on every song: songs on the device, Vyro songs, and the Now Playing screen. Vyro likes are saved on the server for signed-in people, so they follow them to another device, and wait on the device until the connection or the sign-in is there.

LIB-16.note: Pick songs with the system picker; on phones they are copied into the app.

LIB-17.note: Scanning runs in the background with a live count.

SRC-06.note: The mix engine never blends YouTube or license-restricted tracks. YouTube playback itself is not built.

PLY-01.note: Play, pause, seek, next, previous, repeat (off, one, all) and shuffle. Shuffle plays the current song first, and the original order comes back when it is switched off.

PLY-02.note: Notification, lock screen and headset buttons on Android, iOS and macOS, including shuffle and repeat.

PLY-03.note: A queue screen with play next, add, reorder, remove, clear and a history list. Song rows have a menu for "Play next" and "Add to queue".

PLY-04.note: Mini player and full Now Playing screen. Swipe sideways on the mini player or the artwork to skip, and swipe up on the mini player to open Now Playing. Swipe down to close is not built.

PLY-05.note: The audio session is set up for music so calls and other apps are handled by the system. Not tested on a phone.

PLY-06.note: Headset and Bluetooth buttons go through the system media controls.

PLY-20.note: Same work as PLY-02: background playback with system controls on Android, iOS and macOS.

MIX-01.note: Equal-power blend from 1 to 12 seconds (Normal mode is the off setting).

MIX-07.note: Songs on this device are blended. Downloaded online songs do not exist yet.

MIX-08.note: Songs marked not mixable, and YouTube songs, change with a clean cut.

MIX-21.note: Normal and Mixing modes on the player screen.

MIX-22.note: Separate blend lengths for end of song and for next/back.

MIX-23.note: Back restarts the song after 3 seconds, otherwise goes to the earlier song.

DSC-01.note: Songs and artists on Vyro, found even with typos and missing accents, plus songs on the device. Albums, playlists and users cannot be searched yet, because Vyro has no public albums, playlists or user pages.

REC-02.note: Plays are recorded on the device, and plays of Vyro songs are sent to the server when signed in. Private sessions and personalization settings are respected.

SOC-04.note: Follow and unfollow from the artist page. A list of the artists you follow is missing.

UIX-01.note: Midnight, Daylight, AMOLED black and follow-system. The choice is not saved between launches yet.

UIX-07.note: Aurora, Sunset, Forest and Ocean accents.

UIX-12.note: Empty and loading states exist for the Library and statistics, not everywhere.

STA-01.note: Plays, listeners, followers and saves with date ranges, filled by real plays once the app sends them. Saves now include the likes made in the app. Playlist adds are missing.

STA-02.note: Finish rate and skip rate per song. Replays and average listen time are missing.

STA-03.note: Countries only. Cities, age bands and devices are missing.

STA-04.note: Search, recommendations, playlists, charts, shares, library and direct.

STA-07.note: Which songs yours are blended with.

STA-08.note: Last 48 hours hour by hour (shown at any time, not only after a release).

STA-10.note: Groups with fewer than 5 listeners are folded into "Other" to protect privacy.

STA-11.note: The 30-second rule for counting a stream is built. Fraud filtering is missing.

STA-14.note: Monthly listeners and follower numbers exist on the server. There is no artist page screen yet.

STA-16.note: Every headline number shows its change against the period before.

STA-20.note: Plays by hour for the last 48 hours.

PRF-01.note: Header shows the real name and username. No photo yet.

PRF-02.note: 4 weeks, 6 months, this year, all time.

PRF-04.note: Listening streak in the listener's own time zone.

PRF-07.note: Songs blended and new artists found.

PRF-08.note: Saved on the server and shown on the profile; there is no public profile yet to apply it to.

PAY-02.note: Paywall flags exist on the server and default to off. The app does not read them yet.

BKE-01.note: A versioned API. Rate limits exist for sign-in only.

BKE-02.note: A database holds users, artists, songs, follows, saves and plays. Playlists and a separate analytics store are missing.

BKE-13.note: A table of feature switches and a way to read them. There is no admin screen to change them.

BKE-15.note: Plays are stored straight into the database. There is no queue or stream pipeline yet.

QUA-03.note: FLAC and ALAC files are accepted and played by the platform players. Bit-perfect output is not handled.

DEV-01.note: One shared codebase for every platform. A custom native audio engine is not built.

DEV-03.note: The setup script adds the Android service and permissions and the iOS background mode. Battery-optimization handling is missing.

DEV-12.note: One setup script builds Android, iOS, Windows and macOS from one codebase.

SAF-05.note: Deleting an account removes everything, files included; plays stay as anonymous counts. "Download my data" copies a full export (profile, picks, follows, likes, "not interested" choices and the plays linked to the person). The wording and retention periods need a lawyer.

SAF-06.note: Passwords are stored securely hashed. Encryption in transit comes with deployment.

SAF-12.note: Rate limits on sign-in. Nothing for uploads yet.

NFR-10.note: The server has 166 automated checks, all passing. The app's checks are written but have not been run yet.

AUTH-01.note: Phone sign-in works and the screens are built. Codes are not actually sent yet: an SMS service still needs to be connected.

AUTH-03.note: Google and Apple sign-in are checked by the server. The buttons say "not set up" until your Google and Apple developer accounts are connected.

AUTH-04.note: Continue as guest. Profile, artist studio and account actions ask a guest to sign in.

AUTH-05.note: Genres, moods and artists, skippable. "At least three artists" is not enforced because the catalog is still empty.

AUTH-07.note: Reset with an emailed code; signs out every device.

AUTH-09.note: Date of birth at sign-up. Under 13 refused, 13 to 15 need a parent's emailed code, explicit content locked off under 18. Ages need legal review per market.

AUTH-10.note: Private session, "Share my country with artists" (off means plays count without a country), personalized recommendations, and a download of your data are real controls. "Hide my activity" and "Show my listening on my profile" are saved but apply to nothing yet, because friends and public profiles do not exist.

AUTH-15.note: Codes expire after 10 minutes, lock after 5 wrong tries, and are limited to 5 per hour.

AUTH-16.note: Logins last 30 days and renew themselves. Resetting a password signs the person out of every device.

AUTH-17.note: The login is kept in the device's secure storage. With no connection, the app opens with the last saved profile.

AUTH-18.note: Accounts are only linked when the email address is verified. Not yet tried with real Google or Apple accounts.

STU-01.note: Uploads accept MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV, OGG and AIFF files, and the Studio screen picks and uploads them.

STU-04.note: JPEG, PNG and WebP covers up to 5 MB are checked and stored. Size and ratio checks are missing.

STU-06.note: Length, bitrate and sample-rate checks. Clipping, silence and fake-upsample checks are missing.

STU-08.note: Draft, submit for release, withdraw and delete work. Scheduling is missing.

STU-09.note: The server can change title, genre, explicit and blending after publishing. There is no screen for it and no change history.

STU-13.note: Blending can be switched off per song. Download and sharing permissions are stored but have no screen.

STU-19.note: Deleting a song removes its files and keeps its plays in the artist's statistics.

STU-20.note: The 300 MB limit is checked before sending and by the server, and a failed upload is retried on the same song.

SRC-01.note: Songs stream from short-lived secure links and can be played from any point. Adaptive quality is missing.

SRC-02.note: "Vyro" and "On device" badges in search and on Vyro songs. No "Mixable" indicator yet.

SRC-03.note: One search across Vyro and the music on the device, grouped by source. YouTube is not part of it yet.

DSC-04.note: Home shows Continue listening (what you played lately), Picked for you, New on Vyro and Top this week, with a Charts button.

DSC-05.note: Top songs, top artists and rising artists, worldwide or for your own country. An albums chart is missing, because Vyro has no albums yet.

DSC-08.note: Explicit songs are hidden from guests and from anyone with explicit content turned off, in search, new releases, charts and streaming.

BKE-03.note: Files are stored on the server's disk behind a storage layer. Cloud storage and a content delivery network are missing.

BKE-04.note: Lossless uploads get a smaller streaming copy (needs the ffmpeg tool installed on the server). Several bitrates and adaptive streaming are missing.

BKE-05.note: Loudness is measured when a song is uploaded and stored (needs the ffmpeg tool installed on the server).

BKE-07.note: Search uses the database (prefix matches first). Typo tolerance and a search engine are missing.

BKE-08.note: Stream links are signed and expire; altered or expired links are refused.

QUA-02.note: Bitrate, sample-rate and length gates. Fake-upsample detection is missing.

MIX-04.note: Only loudness is measured so far. Beats, key and mix points are missing.

PLY-13.note: Loudness is measured and sent to the app, but not applied to playback yet.

STU-07.note: Songs that sound like ones already on Vyro are put on hold, including re-encoded or trimmed copies. Checking against music released elsewhere is connected, but needs a licensed lookup service to go live.

BKE-06.note: Copies of songs already on Vyro are detected by audio fingerprint, even re-encoded ones. Matching against music released elsewhere needs a licensed lookup service.

ADM-01.note: Roles (listener, moderator, admin) and a record of every decision exist, and the Admin console is built. The record has no screen yet.

ADM-02.note: Approve or reject with a reason the artist is told, one at a time or in bulk.

ADM-03.note: Search artists, verify, suspend and restore. Merging duplicate accounts is missing.

ADM-12.note: Reviewers can listen to a song before deciding, through a private link.

ADM-13.note: Review policy: every song, only new artists, or none. Audio that could not be checked never skips review.

SAF-02.note: A copyright notice takes a song offline at once; the artist can answer with a counter-notice; a reviewer upholds or restores it. The legal wording and time limits need a lawyer.

SAF-03.note: A moderation queue for uploads. Profiles, images and comments are missing.

SAF-14.note: Artists can answer a copyright notice with a counter-notice. Appeals of a rejection or an ownership dispute are missing.

SAF-16.note: Three upheld copyright notices suspend the artist automatically.

SAF-17.note: A suspended account is signed out everywhere, cannot sign in, and its songs are hidden.

STU-21.note: New audio takes a live song offline until it is reviewed again.

REC-18.note: Real listening time per song, including blends.

REC-19.note: Plays made offline or as a guest wait on the device and are sent later. No play is counted twice, and bad data cannot block the rest.

PRF-11.note: Profile combines Vyro listening from the server with music played from the device, streak included. YouTube plays are not part of it yet.

PRF-12.note: Clear listening history on the Account screen.

LYR-01.note: The line being sung is highlighted and scrolled into view.

LYR-02.note: Lyrics open inside the Now Playing screen, and tapping a line jumps to it. There is no separate full-screen view.

LYR-03.note: Lyrics without times are shown as plain text, with verse breaks kept.

LYR-04.note: Songs on the device use a.lrc or.txt file with the same name, or lyrics stored inside the file.

LYR-05.note: Artists add, edit and remove lyrics in the Studio.

LYR-06.note: Lyrics follow the song that is showing, including through a blend. Tempo changes do not exist yet.

LYR-07.note: Listeners report wrong words, timing, offensive or copied lyrics; the artist is told once per person.

LYR-15.note: Lyrics of explicit songs follow the explicit setting, for guests and minors too.

STU-10.note: Artists can write, paste or import.lrc lyrics. There is no tap-to-time editor yet.

PLY-07.note: The queue, shuffle and repeat settings, and the exact place in the song are saved and brought back when the app starts, paused and ready. Nothing loads until play is pressed, so starting needs no connection.

PLY-08.note: A buffering spinner and automatic retries (after 1, 2 and 4 seconds, from where the song stopped) are built. Dropping to a lower quality needs several versions of each song, which do not exist yet.

PLS-01.note: Create, rename, describe and delete playlists, with a cover picture. Playlists are kept on this device.

PLS-02.note: Songs from your own files and from Vyro can be added from any song row or from Now Playing, each shown with a "Vyro" or "Local" badge. YouTube links are not built yet.

PLS-03.note: Drag to reorder, select several songs (remove, add to the queue, add to another playlist), sort by title, artist, date added or length, and remove duplicates.

REC-01.note: Home shows "Picked for you" (from the genres and artists chosen in the taste picker), "Popular in your country" (or on all of Vyro when a country has too little listening), and lists chosen by Vyro's staff. The moods from the picker are not used yet, because songs have no mood. Staff create the lists through the server for now; there is no screen for it.

REC-09.note: Pause personalization (this turns off "Picked for you"), reset recommendations, clear listening history, and "Not interested" for a song or a whole artist.

LIB-06.note: The Liked tab brings songs from the device and from Vyro together, each with a "Local" or "Vyro" badge, and playlists mix both. The Songs, Albums, Artists, Genres and Folders views still show only songs on the device.

LIB-08.note: "Delete from device" in a song's menu, after a confirmation. The song also leaves the queue and every playlist, and if it was playing, playback moves on first. If the file cannot be deleted, the song stays and the person is told. On newer Android versions the system may refuse to delete files outside the app's own folder; that case needs platform code.

DSC-02.note: Suggestions for the first one or two letters, search that forgives typos and accents ("nova wve" finds Nova Wave), and recent searches that can be reused, removed or cleared.

DSC-03.note: Browse by genre, from the Search screen. Mood, activity, decade and language are missing, because songs do not carry those details yet.

DSC-06.note: An artist page with popular songs, all their songs, about, links, similar artists and a follow button. Photo and banner are missing. Reached from search, charts, similar artists and the artist name under any song.
